meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-01 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 56m | Location: Zoom | Attendees: Sofia Tran (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM), Elliot Lyons (Lyons Orthotech Head of MLOps), Dr. Hana Park (CTO), Samir Patel (Infra Lead)
summary: Renewal check-in focused on Lysons Orthotech's desire to expand into EU private VPC/on-prem pilot and add committed capacity. Discussed tradeoffs for latency vs unit cost, SOC2/ISO compliance, KMS integration, and next steps for SOW and pilot kickoff.
topics: Current usage and expected growth (QPS, token mix)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
EU region activation and data residency
Security/compliance: SOC2, ISO, KMS, audit logs
Commercials: SOW, run rate, reserved capacity sizing, contract term
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Marco and Priya are here from my side. Elli — hi?
[00:08] Elliot (Lyons): Yep, hi all. Thanks. Hana and Samir are here too.
[00:12] Marco (Redwood SE): Hey, good to meet. We'll try to keep this focused on the EU private pilot and renewal numbers.
[00:18] Priya (CSM): Quick agenda in the notes, share SOW updates and timeline.
[00:24] Dr. Hana Park: Sounds good. Main thing for us: we want to keep latency under 120ms p95 for our outpatient triage model in EU, and also lock in pricing for the next 12 months.
[00:35] Sofia: Great. Elliot, can you give a quick update on current footprint and growth?
[00:41] Elliot: Sure. We're at ~700 concurrent sessions at peak on hosted, about 8M tokens/day averaged. Growth has been steady, we expect 2.5x by Q2. Sequence length distribution — lots of short queries but some long report gen runs up to 1,200 tokens.
[00:57] Samir: And we've started to see occasional latency spikes when the KV cache flushes, it's a pain.
[01:04] Marco: Right, that ties into the KV cache behavior and prefix caching. In private mode we can tune long-lived pods and the cache retention to avoid those spikes.
[01:12] Elliot: Can Redwood Private meet our audit requirements? We need SOC2, ISO cert evidence, SSO with SAML, and KMS integration.
[01:20] Priya: Yes, we have a SOC2 bundle and ISO docs — I'll share. SSO via SAML and RBAC is supported, and we do KMS/HSM integration patterns. I'll attach the network diagram too.
[01:30] Dr. Hana Park: We also have legal asking about data residency, logs retention, and who can see raw prompts.
[01:36] Sofia: Data residency — in EU private VPC, customer data stays in your VPC and we can set retention policies and restrict access. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[01:44] (slight crosstalk)
[01:46] Elliot: Ok, and on cost — we're evaluating committed reserved capacity vs hosted on-demand. What's the delta?
[01:52] Marco: Committed Dedicated/Private typically reduces per-token compute cost by 35–50% depending on quant and batching. But there's an ops + egress tradeoff. For your mix, we estimate roughly 40% unit cost savings with a 12-month commitment at the tier you're looking at.
[02:06] Samir: What about tail latency for small requests if we batch more? We can't accept big increases.
[02:12] Marco: Continuous batching is workload-aware — we can configure low-latency paths for p95 targets and still batch the background traffic. There's always a small trade; that's what the stress test quantifies.
[02:20] Dr. Hana Park: Requests about private on-prem: we may want an air-gapped option for a narrow set of workloads. Is that realistic?
[02:26] Sofia: Air-gapped is available but adds lead time. For this pilot we recommended EU VPC first, then evaluate on-prem for breadth.
[02:33] Elliot: Timeline-wise we need the pilot live before February. Procurement windows close mid-Jan.
[02:38] Priya: If procurement signs off this month, we can provision a private sandbox in EU in ~3 weeks. On-prem will take longer.
[02:45] (transcription glitch) Speaker 2: uh — sorry — provisioning, pro visioning.
[02:49] Marco: We'll run an internal capacity stress plan — we suggest a 72-hour soak with synthetic traffic and a sample of your production traffic. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 and token costs.
[02:58] Elliot: Good. Please also include GPU memory usage and KV hit rate in logs.
[03:03] Marco: Will do. Also note, when we talk about K V cash — sorry, KV cache — we should instrument cache hit metrics.
[03:10] Samir: On SSO, we need SCIM provisioning and role mapping to our internal teams.
[03:14] Sofia: Supported. We'll include a mapping example.
[03:18] Dr. Hana Park: Any competitors we should be aware of here? We're talking to ApexCloud for an on-premish offering and NimbusServe for a managed dedicated endpoint.
[03:26] Priya: We sometimes see pricing pressure from those vendors; our differentiation is the unified routing and observability — token-level cost breakdowns and the rollout tooling.
[03:35] Elliot: Ok. On the SOW, can Redwood present both a 12-mo committed and a 24-mo staged plan with ramp milestones?
[03:41] Sofia: Yes, we'll include both. We'll also show a Tiered reserved capacity table and a pay-as-you-go fallback.
[03:47] (pause)
[03:49] Samir: For the pilot we need a dedicated contact for incident triage — who should we expect?
[03:53] Priya: I'll be your CSM contact; Marco will be SE lead for the pilot, and we can assign an on-call infra engineer for the pilot window.
[04:00] Elliot: Good. Any gotchas about model quantization or accuracy regressions when changing to more aggressive quant? We need to keep clinical accuracy.
[04:07] Marco: We recommend a conservative quant profile for clinical workloads and an eval suite tied to your prompt sets. Redwood Optimize can run regression alerts against your golden inputs. We'll avoid 8-bit aggressive quant without evals.
[04:19] Dr. Hana Park: Perfect. We'll share a prompt set of 100 edge cases.
[04:24] Sofia: Great. We'll benchmark against that.
[04:27] (ambient noise)
[04:30] Elliot: Who signs the contract on our side? Legal or procurement?
[04:33] Dr. Hana Park: Procurement handles contracts; legal signs off on compliance items. I will loop in procurement lead after this call.
[04:40] Sofia: Recap — we'll send updated SOW with EU VPC pricing and a 12 vs 24 month option, include the pilot plan and a fallback routing playbook, and Marco will schedule the 72-hour stress test. Priya will share SOC2/ISO and network diagrams.
[04:52] Elliot: Thanks. One more Q — can we get a ballpark for total cost of ownership for 2.5x growth?
[04:58] Marco: We'll model that and include token cost delta in the SOW. Expect the cost model in the next 48 hours.
[05:05] Dr. Hana Park: Ok, good. Any blockers left?
[05:08] Samir: No blockers; just awaiting internal procurement OK.
[05:11] Sofia: We'll aim to get artifacts to you tomorrow. Thanks everyone.
[05:15] (call ends)

Note: Transcript includes occasional speech-to-text errors (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache, "sock two" for SOC2). Shared artifacts: SOW draft link (internal): https://redwood.internal/sow/LYONS-EU-DRAFT, SOC2 bundle (link coming), stress-test template: https://redwood.docs/stress-tests/template.pdf
